note: Adapted from the species description of Rhynchotermes piauy by Cancello (1997), originally in English; the alate is unknown (recorded as Imago unknown in the original); figure numbers, type material and locality records are not translated, and soldier measurements are from 10 individuals of the same nest.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier is the smallest described so far in the genus. In R. nyctobius and R. nasutissimus the nasus is much longer and slenderer. The species resembles the minor soldier of R. diphyes, but the nasus is shorter and not inclined downward in lateral view, the mandibles are more strongly incurved and bear fine serrations on the inner apical part, which are absent in R. diphyes.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule pyriform; nasus long, broad at the base and tapering toward the apex, forming a straight line with the posterior part of the head in lateral view. Mandibles long, strongly incurved, pointed apically, with fine serrations, each with a truncate tooth on the inner margin near the apical third, the two teeth about equal in size; when closed, the left mandible overlaps the right along its entire length. Labrum very small, pyriform, concealed beneath the postmentum and the closed mandibles. Anterior margin of the pronotum slightly concave or not concave. Antennae longer than the head, 14-segmented, segment 2 about as long as segment 3, segment 4 the smallest, segment 5 slightly longer than segment 4 and shorter than segments 2 and 3, segments 6 to 14 nearly equal in length to one another and longer than the preceding segments. Postmentum short, slightly square, slightly raised in lateral view. Fore coxal process variable in shape, truncate, conical or otherwise, always with microsculpture. Head with 6 erect setae; nasus without setae, hairy around the aperture. Labrum with 6 setae; pronotum with 4 setae on the anterior margin and some short hairs, the posterior margin with short hairs. Abdominal tergites with 4–6 erect setae on the posterior margin, together with a few short hairs and microsetae; the last three tergites with numerous short hairs directed posteriorly. Sternites with erect setae on the posterior margin, the surface with numerous short hairs directed posteriorly. Fore coxal process with 1 or 2 setae. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2. Measurements (10 soldiers from the same nest): head length 1.43–1.55 mm; nasus length 0.69–0.82 mm; head width 0.69–0.80 mm; pronotum length 0.26–0.35 mm, width 0.35–0.40 mm; hind tibia length 0.73–0.84 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule circular; pronotum as in the soldier. Antennae 14-segmented, segment 2 longer than segment 3, segments 4, 5 and 6 nearly as long as segment 3, segments 7 to 14 slightly longer than the other segments and nearly equal to one another. Fore coxal process very small, circular. Head with some erect setae and short hairs, more numerous than in the soldier. Abdominal tergites with some erect setae on the posterior margin, the surface with short hairs directed posteriorly. Sternites with some anteriorly directed setae and numerous short hairs directed posteriorly. Head yellow, mandibles slightly darker, the teeth and molar region chestnut brown; remainder of the body white, paler than pale yellow.
